findings.message: the pattern matches 10 of 20 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is 'Oct 14 08:00:56 dhcp dhcpd[3163]: DHCPREQUEST for 10.10.5.14 from 02:48:95:17:1b:b5 (ws-ops-004) via eth0'. the pattern matches up to %{IP:src_ip}, which fails on 'for 10.10.5.14 from 02:48:95:17:1b:b5 (w'. %{WORD} matches letters, digits and underscore only - NOT a dot, hyphen, colon or slash. For a hostname use %{HOSTNAME}, for any run of non-space characters use %{NOTSPACE} It also misses lines of other shapes: 'Oct 14 08:01:32 dhcp dhcpd[3163]: DHCPREQUEST for 10.10.1.12 from 02:5a:b6:14:8f:30 (ws-it-002) via eth0'; 'Oct 14 08:02:37 dhcp dhcpd[3163]: DHCPREQUEST for 10.20.7.13 from 02:3f:f8:b2:e4:6f (ws-general-003) via eth0'; 'Oct 14 08:04:06 dhcp dhcpd[3163]: DHCPREQUEST for 10.20.7.12 from 02:62:80:94:c7:13 (ws-general-002) via eth0'. If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.
